title: Fluent Logistics Routing Configuration
business: Logistics providers managing complex, multi-stop delivery routes.
problem: Configuration code often becomes deeply nested and difficult to read when applying multiple sequential filters or transformations to a route object, leading to maintenance overhead.
solution: Method chaining allows developers to invoke a sequence of operations on a route object by returning the receiver instance from each method, creating a fluent, readable interface that mimics a natural language configuration flow.
steps: Define the base Route object to hold delivery parameters.
Implement configuration methods that modify internal state.
Ensure each configuration method returns the 'this' reference to the caller.
Construct the final route by appending method calls in a single statement.
Verify the final state of the object after the chain completes.
outcome: Improved code readability and reduced boilerplate when setting up complex delivery constraints.
limitation: Debugging becomes more difficult because stack traces may not clearly identify which specific link in the chain failed; check this by inspecting the object state before and after the chain execution.
